0.0.n: This standard evening greeting ends with は, pronounced わ.

1.0.n: Read きょう here; は makes it the topic.

1.1.n: Marks 今日 as the topic, setting the time frame for what follows.

1.2.n: The first part of the store name セブン-イレブン.

1.4.n: The second part of the store name セブン-イレブン.

1.5.n: Marks 7-Eleven as the place where the product was released.

2.0.n: Read にがつ; a number followed by 月 names a month.

2.1.n: Read とおか, the special reading for the tenth day of a month.

2.2.n: Marks February 10th as the specific date of release.

2.3.n: 発売する becomes 発売された, a past passive form describing what happened to the product.

2.4.n: 発売された comes before this noun to describe which product it is.

3.0.n: A polite way to refer to the item being shown, written in katakana here for emphasis.

3.1.n: Marks コチラ as the item the speaker will eat or drink.

3.2.n: The polite form of いただく, a humble way to say eat or drink.

0.tip: こんばんは is a fixed greeting; its final は is pronounced わ.

1.tip: The sentence continues: で connects the store to the product's release in the next line.

2.tip: Japanese puts descriptions before nouns: 発売された新商品 means a new product that was released.

3.lit: This one, I will humbly eat or drink.
3.tip: With an item marked by を, いただきます states what the speaker will consume, rather than just offering a mealtime greeting.
